skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

4. // hal::platform::microvm — Specifications (target: `gva_to_gpa`)
5. //
6. // The in-scope facet of this module is the MicroVM platform's guest-virtual →
7. // guest-physical address translation (`gva_to_gpa`). It is a free function
8. // (`#[inline(always)] pub fn gva_to_gpa(gva: usize) -> usize`) — pure, total and
9. // deterministic — that reads/writes no global state. There is therefore no
10. // caller-observable *state* to model, only a caller-observable *mathematical
11. // map*. The honest View for this scope is a stateless (unit) View whose content
12. // is a single pure translation function plus the algebraic properties the caller
13. // relies on. See `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-hal-platform-microvm/view_design.md`.
14. 
15. verus! {
16. 
17. // Caller-visible abstraction of the MicroVM platform's address-translation
18. // facet. The translation `gva_to_gpa` is a pure, stateless function, so this
19. // View carries no fields: there is no mutable abstract state a caller observes
20. // across calls. The substance of the abstraction is the spec function
21. // `spec_gva_to_gpa` and its properties, defined below on this type.
22. pub struct MicrovmTranslationView {}
23. 
24. impl MicrovmTranslationView {
25.     // Well-formedness of the translation facet. The facet is stateless, so there
26.     // is no internal bookkeeping to constrain; well-formedness (totality,
27.     // determinism, injectivity) is structural — a property of `spec_gva_to_gpa`,
28.     // a total Verus spec function — not an invariant over mutable fields.
29.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
30.         true
31.     }
32. 
33.     // Abstract guest-virtual → guest-physical translation as a mathematical map
34.     // over addresses. On the MicroVM platform the guest address space is flat
35.     // and identity-mapped, so this is the identity. Addresses are modeled as
36.     // `nat` (raw, non-negative machine addresses in spec world). `open` because
37.     // identity is the caller-relevant MicroVM contract: callers depend on the
38.     // result equaling the input to walk distinct frames.
39.     pub open spec fn spec_gva_to_gpa(self, gva: nat) -> nat {
40.         gva
41.     }
42. 
43.     // Injectivity of the translation over the address space: distinct guest
44.     // virtual addresses yield distinct guest physical addresses. This is what
45.     // lets `book_mmio_regions` advance `start` by `FRAME_SIZE` and be sure it
46.     // walks distinct physical frames (no aliasing / double-booking).
47.     pub open spec fn injective(self) -> bool {
48.         forall|a: nat, b: nat|
49.             #![trigger self.spec_gva_to_gpa(a), self.spec_gva_to_gpa(b)]
50.             self.spec_gva_to_gpa(a) == self.spec_gva_to_gpa(b) ==> a == b
51.     }
